meta.title: The Sentence That Went First
meta.theme: how two separate conveniences at the ends of a telegraph wire settled the shape of the news paragraph

format.format_verified: 2026-09: five sentences, TITA, +3 with no negative marking, consistent in released papers 2016 to 2025; re-verify against each new official paper

traps.description: The outlier is quiet, balanced and generous, so a reader listening for a raised voice hears no shift at all; it also uses the paragraph's own pair of terms, outcome and circumstances. The decoy is the sentence that crosses to the editors' end of the wire, which looks like a change of subject at the moment the story seemed settled.

meta.learning_objective: hold a narrative's purpose steady and see that a sentence which defends what the narrative describes has stopped telling the story and begun settling an argument

quality.adversarial_review: The rival is the sentence about editors and the compositor: it crosses to the other end of the wire and supplies a second, unrelated motive, so a reader following one causal thread will call it a branch. It stays because the closing sentence counts two conveniences, one at each end, and without the editors' convenience there is only one. The sentence weighing what was lost is the intruder: every other sentence reconstructs why people did what they did, and this one delivers a verdict on the result, answering a complaint the paragraph has never recorded anyone making.

source.usage_note: Original composition in CAT register for CAT OS. General account of the origins of front-loaded news writing; no specific text adapted. Personal study only.

meta.reviewer_notes: An elite stance item where the shift is a defence rather than an attack. The core narrates causes without judging the outcome, and the outlier's calm reasonableness is exactly what makes it hard to catch.

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: Editors at the receiving end found the arrangement convenient for an unrelated reason: a report built that way could be cut from the bottom by a compositor who had not read it.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: Little was lost in the exchange, since a reader who wants the outcome is served at once and a reader who wants the circumstances need only read on.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: Correspondents filing by telegraph paid by the word and worked on lines that failed without warning, often in the middle of a sentence.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: The habit that grew out of this was to send the outcome first and the circumstances afterwards, so that a dispatch broken off at any point was still a dispatch.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: Two conveniences, one at each end of the wire, settled the shape of the news paragraph for a century, long after the wires themselves had been taken down.

builder.prompt: Build the four-sentence story of how the news paragraph got its shape, from the failing wire to the century that followed. The sentence that has stopped narrating and started judging is your answer.

explanation.spine_note: The core tells one causal story in four steps. It opens with the conditions of filing by telegraph, priced by the word and liable to break, then gives the habit those conditions produced. The third step crosses to the other end of the wire, where the same habit turned out to suit editors for a quite different reason, and the fourth counts the two conveniences and states how long their accident lasted. Conditions, habit, second motive, outcome.

core_roles.label: C
core_roles.why_here: It supplies the two pressures the habit answers, cost per word and a line that can fail mid-sentence, and nothing later makes sense without them.

core_roles.label: D
core_roles.why_here: 'Grew out of this' takes those pressures as its cause, and the sentence states the practice the whole story is about.

core_roles.label: A
core_roles.why_here: It moves the story to the receiving end and adds a second, independent motive, which is what turns a wartime expedient into a settled form.

core_roles.label: E
core_roles.why_here: It counts the two motives just narrated and carries the story past the technology that produced it, which is where a story of an origin has to end.

links.explanation: 'Grew out of this' points at the conditions of the previous sentence and makes the habit their consequence rather than their successor.
'The arrangement' substitutes for the habit just described, and 'the receiving end' answers the sending end the story has been standing at.
'Two conveniences, one at each end' counts the motive just given together with the earlier one, so the closing sentence needs both.

explanation.violation_named: The four core sentences reconstruct why people did what they did. The odd sentence assesses what the result was worth, and finds in its favour. That is a change of stance, from explaining a practice to defending it, and the paragraph has not opened a case that anything needs defending from.
explanation.why_it_breaks: A verdict needs a charge. Nothing in the story says the form was criticised, so the sentence answers an objection the paragraph never records, and the one after it is busy counting motives rather than weighing costs. It also stops the clock: the narrative moves from the wire to the newsroom to the century after, and the verdict belongs to no moment in that sequence.
explanation.trap_exposed: The camouflage is good manners. The stray sentence is balanced, unexcited and even-handed, and it recycles the paragraph's own pair of terms, outcome and circumstances, so a reader listening for a shift in volume hears none. The decoy is the crossing to the editors, which looks like a digression at the very point where the story seemed complete, and is in fact the second half of the explanation the closing sentence adds up.

exclusion_analysis.label: C
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: It is the only sentence that never mentions the shape of a report, so a reader matching on the paragraph's subject finds nothing in it to hold.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without it the habit has no cause, and 'grew out of this' points at nothing, so the story begins in the middle of its own explanation.

exclusion_analysis.label: D
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: It reads like a definition of a writing convention rather than an event, so a reader sorting the story into moments may not find a moment for it.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without it the paragraph never states the practice it is explaining, and the editors' convenience is a convenience about nothing.

exclusion_analysis.label: A
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: It changes place, changes actors and offers a motive that has nothing to do with broken wires, which makes it look like a branch off the causal line.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without it the closing count of two conveniences is wrong, and the story explains why correspondents wrote this way but not why the form outlasted them.

exclusion_analysis.label: E
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: It summarises rather than narrates, and its reach across a century is unlike the close focus of everything before it.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without it the two motives are never brought together and the story stops at a printing-house convenience, with the outcome it was leading to unstated.

explanation.detection_habit: Ask whether the four sentences are explaining or evaluating, and then check each sentence against that answer. A verdict, however gently phrased, needs a dispute to settle, and a narrative rarely contains one.

mentor.challenge: Five calm sentences about how news came to be written outcome first. One of them has quietly finished thinking and is telling you what to conclude.
mentor.takeaway: A story explains why something happened. The moment a sentence tells you it was no great loss, it has joined a different conversation.
